video_title: Denver Nuggets' 2ND APRON WOES with BOBBY MARKS

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks on how CBA rules impact team roster decisions
quotes.excerpt: you don't realize the rules until it impacts your team. Like that's the biggest thing
quotes.quote: People think, listen, people think it's every summer people think this is the new CBA. Where did these rules come from? And I was like, oh, in 2023, they've been here. But it's funny, Grace, you don't realize the rules until it impacts your team. Like that's the biggest thing. New York was never bothered by the apron until all of a sudden you make some trades. Denver has kind of skirted a little bit under it and everything, but now you're in the weeds of the second apron.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks on LeBron James joining the Philadelphia 76ers
quotes.excerpt: Ever since Luka, I've been my surprise-ness has gotten down a notch
quotes.quote: You know it's funny, Grace, ever since Luka, I've been my surprise-ness has gotten down a notch and stuff. Luka trade I was like, holy blank, right? I know where I was, I know what time of the day it was. I knew I was in my closet because I was packing for LA for trade deadline. I knew everywhere I was. LeBron, I was sitting at my desk doing work on that Friday. Not totally caught off guard, but I thought Philly was probably third out of the teams. I thought it was going to be one of the three Eastern Conference teams: Cleveland, Miami, and Philadelphia.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks on Lonnie Walker IV's non-guaranteed contract with Denver
quotes.excerpt: It's a non-guaranteed contract. It's funny, the Exhibit 9 has come into play
quotes.quote: It's a non-guaranteed contract. It's funny, the Exhibit 9 has come into play. So anyone for you Denver Nuggets fans out there, an Exhibit 9, so it's a non-guaranteed contract. It's funny, the Exhibit 9 has come into play. I think when I was with the Nets, we had, so we had Darvin Ham, this is Darvin Ham as a player. And Darvin Ham got injured in training camp and we were basically on the hook for his salary until he got healthy. So the Exhibit 9 protects the Nuggets in this case. So if Lonnie Walker comes in and tears his ACL, hopefully he doesn't, that they're only on the hook for $15,000.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks on Nikola Jokic's contract extension decision
quotes.excerpt: He was extension eligible a year ago, elected not to sign the extension
quotes.quote: He was extension eligible a year ago, elected not to sign the extension and basically came out because it would give him more spending power. It was a business decision to sign the extension this summer. Last year he was extension eligible for like three years. This year it's like four for $275 million, somewhere around there. And this year it's now we're here again, and it's a business decision. Now it's the ability to opt out of his contract next summer and then sign a five-year $360 million deal with Denver, which would be the largest in NBA history.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks on the complexity of a Peyton Watson sign-and-trade
quotes.excerpt: Denver being above the second apron complicates a sign-and-trade for Peyton in even more
quotes.quote: Denver being above the second apron complicates a sign-and-trade for Peyton in even more than it already was because of lots of other rules. It's one of those sneaky little rules that only pop up in certain situations. Right? Because as we've talked about it, certainly with Denver, sign-and-trades are hard. Does a player want to commit to three years on a sign-and-trade? Does Peyton Watson want to commit to three years $45 million, just giving an example, and be on that contract for three years?

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks on the danger of restricted free agency
quotes.excerpt: It's one of those sneaky little rules that only pop up in certain situations
quotes.quote: It's one of those sneaky little rules that only pop up in certain situations. Because as we've talked about it, certainly with Denver, sign-and-trades are hard. The danger comes is when you don't get a deal done and you go into restricted free agency. And when the market is condensed and there's only three teams with cap space in Brooklyn, Chicago, and the Lakers, and the Lakers are forced to send two unprotected first and two pick swaps to get Walker Kessler who was restricted free agency.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks on the rarity of rookie extensions
quotes.excerpt: Kobe White goes for three for 74. And that's a big reason why, you know, like those contracts don't happen as much
quotes.quote: Kobe White goes for three for 74. And that's a big reason why, you know, like those contracts don't happen as much. Like when Gary Trent Jr. contract comes, I'm just writing on my whiteboard, and he signs for whatever four for 64 and it's the 10th biggest contract and all four years are guaranteed and he averaged eight points per game last year and shot 37% from the field, people are like, what the F is going on in Milwaukee? And so then you kind of go, oh, he's just signed back-to-back contracts for the minimum basically.

quotes.speaker: Grace Jean
quotes.summary_phrase: Peyton Watson's contract extension and roster role in Denver
quotes.excerpt: the question for me is really like what's the length of the deal

text_blocks.speaker: Grace Jean
text_blocks.text: It seems like they want to keep Peyton Watson. The question for me is really like what's the length of the deal. On last week's show, I suggested something like a three-year deal with a team option, but I'm sure Peyton would prefer a player option. The compromise there is you think you've got the upside, play over the next couple of seasons, you'll have the option to re-enter free agency, you'll be in your prime, you're still young, you can go get the number that you want.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: Usually we look at it in three-year windows. You've got Cam Johnson who is a free agent next year, right? Are you ready to lose both those guys? That's the question, and who are you replacing them with? You're in the apron no matter what. I always say there's no harm going into the apron, the harm is when you're there for two more years.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Denver's financial constraints and the lack of tradable assets
quotes.excerpt: the problem with Denver is the lack of tradable assets
quotes.quote: The problem with Denver is the lack of tradable assets. If you've got three seconds that you have available to move, you've got no first, we know you got some swaps there, but what are you doing if you're trying to shed all this money? And then does shedding money help you compete? That's the other thing. Are you moving off players that actually help you on the court for the greater good of financial reasons?

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Nuggets likely to remain in the second apron next season
quotes.excerpt: I think they'll be in the second apron this year. I think they'll stay in it
quotes.quote: I think they'll be in the second apron this year. I think they'll stay in it. It's hard. We saw Boston do it and it was a gradual process. They took a pickaxe and chopped away at the ice block. It took them like five different moves to get under there. Trading a $23 million player for a $15 million player, yeah, you can potentially do that and get you under, and it depends on where Peyton is and everything like that.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Bobby Marks' evaluation of a $20 million salary for Peyton Watson
quotes.excerpt: I think 20 is a solid number
quotes.quote: I think 20 is a solid number. The non-tax is 15. If you're paying 5 million above that, I think where his role is, and as I said, I want guys on their contract. I don't want one of my starters and one of my six men becoming free agents next year.

quotes.speaker: Grace Jean
quotes.summary_phrase: Nuggets roster size and potential league-wide roster rule violations
quotes.excerpt: is there any discussion in league-wide circles about how close teams have been to violating the minimum roster rule

text_blocks.speaker: Grace Jean
text_blocks.text: Denver appears to be yet again a team that is looking to enter the season with only 14 roster spots filled in order to deal with their financial realities of being a repeater team. Is there any discussion in league-wide circles about how close teams have been to violating the minimum league-wide roster rule? The league has to maintain an average of 14 and a half standard roster players across a season, and basically if too many teams only have 14, which is the minimum number that a team has to have, for too long, the Players Association can give notice to the league to fix it or they take away the third two-way spot.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: Yeah, I think there's certainly antennas are up as far as with that ruling and where the number is going to be. I think antennas are up also like the strict rules as far as keeping below 14 players. If you have 13 players on your roster, you can only go two weeks at a time below that 14 number and can't be more than a total of 28 days.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Expansion and the next CBA alignment
quotes.excerpt: it feels like expansion is being aligned with the next CBA
quotes.quote: It feels like expansion is being aligned with the next CBA. It feels like that's where we're heading a little bit if you're going to start an expansion team in 28-29 or even 29-30. That basically aligns where the CBA is. I think with expansion, just because we haven't seen it in so long, the unknown with the rules are. It's going to be interesting how teams sign players, because you're probably keeping an eye on what I can protect and what I can't protect here.
